direction.NOTE: the left accent bar on each metric tile is a FIVE-band scale (emerald <30, violet <50, sky <70, amber <85, red ≥85 — web/lib/usageColorUtils.ts:8-20), so this fleet legitimately shows violet and sky bars on camera. Don't grade or re-time the shot to force a green-to-red look; the revoiced line describes headroom vs pinned, not a hue ramp.

beats.title: the one-glance promise
beats.screen_note: slow zoom into one machine card — status pill and last heartbeat, then the metric tiles in their real order (cpu, ram, disk, gpu, network) with sparklines behind them, then the displays section, then the process list.

direction.SCREEN: slow zoom into one machine card — status pill and last heartbeat, then the metric tiles in their real order (cpu, ram, disk, gpu, network) with sparklines behind them, then the displays section, then the process list.
direction.NOTE: the spoken word "memory" here maps to the tile the UI labels "ram" (MachineCardView.tsx:506) — audio is unchanged, so frame the zoom on the card as a whole rather than resting on that one label. Also: `dashboard-mixed-states` seeds NO processes (fixtures.ts writeMachineMetrics has no `metrics.processes`), so a card renders the empty "add process" button instead of a process list. Seed processes on the focus machine before recording, or the last clause of this beat has nothing on screen.
